subject: Proposal: reserved capacity uplift + warm-start policy for renewal
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Linda Huang <linda.huang@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: reserved capacity uplift + warm-start policy for renewal

Hi Linda —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. As part of Acme's renewal (REDW-9021) we sketched a proposal that should address the throughput spikes you've been seeing during peak batch runs and the need to keep latency bounded for interactive flows. High-level:

- Reserved pool: add 8x A100 GPUs to your Dedicated pool (bringing the reserved total to 24 GPUs).
- Autoscaling bounds: min_replicas=2, max_replicas=24.
- Warm-start pool (warm_pool): reserve 4 replicas kept ready to accept traffic without cold-starts.
- Scale-up lag target: 30s (we can set to 45s if you prefer a less aggressive ramp).
- Throughput commitment: we can guarantee 45k tokens/min sustained across the pool during working-hours windows; measured at the token-level with our telemetry.

Notes on billing: the warm_pool is billed at a reduced reserved rate (40% of a full active replica) in this plan — effectively a soft-reservation that keeps KV/cache primed. I'll include a cost delta in the follow-up.

Attached is a short draft capacity addendum that wires these numbers into a contract-friendly format (capacity-addendum-draft.pdf). If this aligns with Acme's needs, next steps would be: procurement confirmation of the uplift, legal review of the addendum, and a two-week activation lead to provision the extra GPUs and seed the warm pool.

Questions for you:
1) Is the 4-replica warm pool acceptable (or would you prefer 2/6)?
2) Do you need a different scale-up lag target for cost reasons?
3) Any procurement/PO timelines we should know about before we draft a signature-ready addendum?

I'll loop in Markus and Marissa for pricing and legal alignment.

Thanks,
Dylan
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: capacity-addendum-draft.pdf (PDF, 145KB)
From: Linda Huang <linda.huang@acmecorp.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 10:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: reserved capacity uplift + warm-start policy for renewal

Dylan —

Appreciate the quick summary. A few clarifying questions from our side after an internal sync with SRE and procurement: 

- Can you provide a delta estimate (monthly) showing incremental cost for the 8x A100s + warm_pool as you described? We need line items: reserved GPU, warm_pool billing, expected data egress, and any additional monitoring/ops charges.
- How does the warm_pool behave during long idle periods? Will we still be billed at the reduced rate if warm_pool isn't used for >48 hours?
- If we keep the warm_pool at 4 replicas but only need 2 at peak, can it automatically scale down after X hours? How are scale-down windows configured?

Procurement also asked whether you can attach a simple SLA addendum with latency/throughput SLOs and credits for missed targets — that will help fast-track internal sign-off.

I've attached our internal requirements spreadsheet so you can validate the numbers on your end (acme_internal_requirements.xlsx). We also prefer DocuSign routing to legal once the addendum is ready.

Thanks,
Linda
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Corporation

Subject: Re: Proposal: reserved capacity uplift + warm-start policy for renewal

Linda —

Thanks for the detailed questions. Answers and an initial cost breakdown below (numbers are approximate until procurement confirms billing account):

1) Monthly delta estimate (illustrative):
   - 8x A100 reserved pool: $36,000/month
   - Warm_pool (4 replicas billed at 40%): $5,760/month
   - Monitoring & Ops premium (24/7 on-call routing + extended retention): $1,200/month
   - Estimated egress: $300/month
   = Total incremental: ~$43,260/month

2) Warm_pool idle behavior: warm_pool replicas remain allocated and are billed at the reduced reserved rate regardless of short idle periods. If warm_pool is unused for >30 days we can convert to a standby reservation at an even lower rate, but that requires a formal change order. For your >48-hour idle question: yes, you'll still be billed the reduced rate during that window.

3) Scale-down behavior: the warm_pool is independent of autoscaling for active replicas. Active replicas can scale down to min_replicas (2) based on an inactivity window. We recommend a 20-minute idle window for scale-down to avoid thrashing; that parameter is configurable per route. The warm_pool will not auto-shrink below the configured warm_pool size (4) unless we execute a change order.

SLA addendum: attached is SLA-addendum-v1.pdf with latency SLOs (p95 < 220ms for interactive flows during working hours) and a throughput guarantee (45k tokens/min sustained as noted). Credit tiers are included for missed throughput/latency targets.

Operational timeline: once procurement confirms, we can provision the 8 GPUs and seed the warm_pool within ~10 business days. Final activation depends on a signed addendum and a valid billing PO.

Links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345/REDW-9021
DocuSign pre-fill: https://docusign.com/req/abc-REDW-9021

I'll put together a signature-ready PDF and cost CSV so procurement can route it.
